subject: Discovery recap: Inference costs & success criteria (FinBot)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.g@finbot.ai>, Priya Anand <priya@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Discovery recap: Inference costs & success criteria (FinBot)

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the intro call today. Quick recap from our side so we have a shared record and clear next steps. Overall you flagged strong cost pressure on inference and a need to both control unit economics and preserve response quality for interactive flows. Key points below: 

Pain points / context
- Monthly inference spend: ~$45k today (Samir confirmed on call) — spikes are driving the unpredictable bill.
- Current infra: self-hosted A100 fleet behind a k8s gateway; custom autoscaler but cold-starts and tail latency remain an issue. No standardized prefix/KV caching.
- Workload: mix of interactive chat (low latency SLO) and async batch reranking. Peak burstiness up to ~4k qps for short windows.

Success criteria (what you said success looks like)
- Reduce per-token inference cost by ~2.5–3x vs today while keeping overall quality within current tolerance.
- 95th percentile latency <= 300ms for interactive traffic at normal load (with acceptable graceful degradation during peaks).
- Ability to support ~5k qps peak with predictable costs and autoscaling behavior.

Openness / constraints
- Quantization: team is open to int8 / 4-bit experiments but needs regression monitoring — accuracy is important for core user flows.
- Batching/caching: want prefix/KV caching and workload-aware batching; cannot accept batching that consistently increases p95 for interactive queries.

Next steps (agreed)
1) Technical deep-dive / infra workshop with Ben (inference engineer) to share trace-level requirements and run a short benchmark. Ben to propose test harness and what telemetry we need.
2) FinBot to share sample request distribution (qps profile + typical sequence lengths) and any eval prompt sets for regression checks.
3) Redwood to run a small pilot (1–2 weeks) to quantify unit economics tradeoffs (batching, cache hit-rate, and quantization impacts).
4) Share cost-model template + demo guide (attached) and a short proposal after the pilot.

Attachments: redwood-infer-demo-guide.pdf, cost-model-template.xlsx

I'll loop Ben in separately to schedule the deep-dive — is Thursday morning PT still good for your team?

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Samir Gupta <samir.g@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Anand <priya@finbot.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 20:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Inference costs & success criteria (FinBot)

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the key numbers from our side: current inference spend is ~USD 45k/month, target budget we'd be happy with is sub-USD 20k/month while keeping quality losses to a minimum. Peak observed qps is 4.2k during campaign bursts; normal steady-state qps is ~700. Typical sequence lengths for interactive flows are 30–80 tokens; reranking jobs have much longer contexts (200–800 tokens).

We're open to exploring quantization (int8 first; 4-bit if quality holds). We do need an eval plan so we can verify regressions on core prompts — I'll share a small prompt set after this note.

Thursday morning PT works for a 45–60 minute deep-dive — prefer 10:00am PT if that slot is available. Ben's involvement is great; he'll need access to sample traffic traces/telemetry and a runbook for the benchmark.

Appreciate the attachments. We'll get the prompt/eval set and request distribution over to you by EOD Friday.

Best,
Samir Gupta
Head of ML Ops, FinBot, Inc
samir.g@finbot.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.g@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priya Anand <priya@finbot.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Inference costs & success criteria (FinBot)

Thanks Samir — 10:00am PT Thursday works. I'll send a calendar invite in a minute.

Ben — can you share the test harness repo and a short checklist of telemetry we need (CPU/GPU utilization, batch sizes, kv cache hit rates, latency p50/p95/p99, token counts, and cost per token breakdown)? If you can also include a runnable benchmark script that we can execute against a small sample of their traffic traces that would speed the pilot.

Samir / Priya — attaching the cost-model-template.xlsx and the demo guide again for reference; I also dropped a HubSpot link to the deal notes. After the deep-dive we'll propose a 1–2 week pilot to run the benchmark and verify quantization/regression results.

Next immediate actions:
- Marissa: calendar invite + pilot proposal outline (today)
- FinBot: share prompt eval set + request distribution (by EOD Fri)
- Ben: test harness + telemetry checklist (before deep-dive)

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the deep-dive.

—
